Subject: Renewal question: adding isolated analytics cluster + fanout for new PI workload

Soojin,

Quick context: our renewal for the Private deployment is coming up (July 15). We expect a new PHI/PI-heavy analytics stream to start in Q4 and want to accelerate isolation planning now rather than after renewal. Two asks:

- Add a dedicated isolated cluster (EU/US split not required initially) for PI processing with strict network isolation and KMS-backed keys.
- Ability to fanout a secondary read-only cluster for analytics (burst capacity) during monthly reporting windows.

Can you share high-level timelines and whether this would require a term amendment or a separate addendum? Also attaching a short doc with our security checklist.

Thanks,
Asha Narayanan
Head of Cloud Operations
MedPulse Health

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear brief and the checklist. Pushed to loop in Kimberly (pricing/contracts) and Ben (on-prem/dedicated ops) so we can size and confirm the contract path.

High level from product/ops side:
- Adding an isolated cluster for PI processing is feasible as an amendment to your current Private terms; we can treat it as a "segmentation add-on" rather than a full re-provision. Typical lead time: 6–8 weeks for provisioning + validation (can be accelerated with a one-time engineering expedite).
- Fanout (read-only analytics cluster) can be delivered as a scheduled burst capacity configuration; we recommend a small warm standby cluster + autoscale policy to handle monthly peaks.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal cost/pricing + SLA impact assessment (cc: Kimberly, Ben)
2) Draft mutual action plan with milestones for provisioning and validation (I will attach an initial MAP)
3) Contract amendment draft (Kimberly) and signature routing (DocuSign)

I attached a first-pass MAP for your review — includes timeline options and the expedite path.

Thanks — will follow up with numbers by EOD tomorrow.

Subject: Re: Renewal question: adding isolated analytics cluster + fanout for new PI workload

Soojin — reviewed the MAP and Asha's checklist. Quick pricing/contract notes: 

- Baseline: add one dedicated isolated cluster (4x A100 equiv) = +25% to existing committed capacity; we can price as a monthly add-on to the Private fee.
- Fanout/burst cluster: recommend a warm standby (2x A100 equiv) with scheduled autoscale; billable as "burst reserve" hours plus a small provisioning fee.
- Term implication: since this is a capacity + isolation change tied to renewal, we should offer a 12-month amendment aligned to the July 15 renewal date. If MedPulse signs for 24 months, we can offer 10% uplift discount on the new cluster baseline.

Questions for Ben: any ops constraints on a same-region isolated cluster with KMS integration? Also, can we commit to a 6-week standard lead time or do we need to plan for 8?

I'll draft the amendment language and include a pricing table; Soojin, please confirm whether the discount conversation is something to present now or wait for the internal executive approval on their side.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Contracts & Pricing
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal question: adding isolated analytics cluster + fanout for new PI workload

Kimberly / Soojin — ops check:
- KMS/HSM integration: standard for Private deployments; we need customer-managed key access and an IAM mapping session (we'll run a short onboarding checklist).
- Network isolation: we can deploy the isolated cluster in the customer's VPC with private peering and no public egress for the PI cluster; will require MedPulse to approve VPN/BGP config and some firewall rules.
- Lead time: baseline 6 weeks if we get signed amendment + approved infra ticket within 5 business days. If they request accelerated provisioning within 2 weeks, we can do it but will require an expedite fee and an engineer-on-call during cutover.

Sizing note: if they expect heavy monthly reporting spikes (10–12x baseline token throughput) the warm standby should be sized at least 3x baseline; otherwise autoscale cold-start could impact SLAs. Recommend we offer two burst profiles in the pricing table (Moderate and High).

I'll prepare an ops checklist and signal the team to reserve an expedited slot week-of-July-12 in case they choose the fast path.

— Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
